subject: Biotechnology
title: How Monoclonal Antibodies Work
description: A quick win: understand How Monoclonal Antibodies Work.

hook.text: Antibodies are Y-shaped proteins that lock onto targets — monoclonal antibodies are armies of identical copies.

buildup.text: Each monoclonal antibody recognizes one specific epitope — a tiny patch on a protein surface.

discovery.text: Binding the target can block a receptor, flag a cell for destruction, or neutralize a toxin.

twist.text: The first monoclonals were mouse antibodies — human immune systems attacked them. Humanization solved this.

climax.text: Over 100 monoclonal antibodies are now approved — treating cancer, autoimmune disease, and infections.

punchline.text: One target, one antibody — precision medicine in protein form.

quiz.question: Why did early mouse monoclonal antibodies need to be humanized?
options: Mouse antibodies were too large to inject into humans
The human immune system recognized mouse proteins as foreign and attacked them
Mouse antibodies could not bind human disease targets
